extracted.intended_audience: KIPO patent examiners; patent applicants and agents interacting with KIPO
extracted.subtask_description: Procedural and substantive guidelines for Korean patent examination: citation format, period extensions/shortenings, treatment of written arguments and amendments, requests for reference documents, additional searches, and deferral/processing-period extensions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Citation format — periodicals and non-periodicals
rubrics_metrics.description: Order of description when citing publications: Name of Author, Title of Thesis, Title of Publication. Location of Publication: Publisher. Publication Date, Number of Volumes, Number of Issues, Page No.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Punctuation: author/title/thesis separated with period (.), location and publisher distinguished with colon (:), period after publisher, others by comma. Title of publication generally not abbreviated. Volumes/issues stated as 'Volume oo, No.oo' (English: 'Vol. oo, No. oo'). Where publication date can substitute volume number, volume/issue may be omitted. Publication date refers to the date inscribed on documents; if day not inscribed, month/year suffices. For unclear publication dates, state the documents with a clear explanation. If publisher poses no risk of misunderstanding, publisher name may be omitted. If location not well known, follow it with country separated by comma; for publications published in Korea, omit location. Name of author and thesis title can be omitted if unnecessary. Pages: indicate with 'pp.' before numeral; for consecutive pages use hyphen (-) between first and last page, for non-consecutive use comma. Title of publication in italics; for translations, write original language with Korean in parenthesis.

rubrics_metrics.name: Citation format — books
rubrics_metrics.description: Order for book citation: Name of Author (or Editor). Book Title. Location of Publication: Publisher. Publication Date, Number of Volume, No. of Edition, and No. of Page.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: For translated books include Name of Translator after author/editor. Use period (.) between author and book title, colon (:) between location and publisher, period after publisher, others by comma. For lectures, collective works, or series, state title of lecture/series and number of volumes before book title. Book title in italics. If edition number not indicated on the book, it may be omitted. For books published in Korea, omit location. Page numbers: use 'pp.' before numerals; rules for plural pages follow periodicals rules.

rubrics_metrics.name: Citation of parts used as grounds for rejection
rubrics_metrics.description: When a part of a publication is cited as grounds for rejection, include page number or drawing number in parentheses to clearly stipulate which part is used.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Example citation forms are given (journal with vol/issue and pp. or book with edition and pp.). This ensures precise identification of the cited portion used to support a rejection.

rubrics_metrics.name: Citation of electronic documents
rubrics_metrics.description: When citing electronic documents (CD-ROM, internet, online DB), state general information of the cited document along with type of search medium (in braces), search date (in braces after publication date) and search site (URL).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Example format: [online], February 2001, [Search on July 15, 2010], Internet: <URL: http://...>. Examiner should include medium type and exact search date/site so the electronic source can be identified and verified.

rubrics_metrics.name: Extension/shortening of designated period — general principle
rubrics_metrics.description: The Commissioner of KIPO or an examiner may, upon request, shorten or extend a designated period, or extend the period ex officio.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Decisions to shorten or extend must be made in a way that does not unlawfully violate the interests of interested parties involved in the relevant procedure.

rubrics_metrics.name: Extension and approval of designated period for substantive examination
rubrics_metrics.description: Procedures and limits for requesting and approving extensions of periods designated for substantive examination.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: An extension can be requested once or twice a month; requests under one month treated as one month. Except for the period for written-argument submission, a request is deemed approved on its filing date, but the examiner may approve only a partial period and must deliver a warning notification for any disapproved remainder. For extension requests of the written-argument-designated period, if the extended expiry is within four months of the original expiry, the request is deemed approved on filing; beyond that the examiner reviews reasons. After approval, the examiner must send a written notification explaining the approval and informing that additional extension requires a petition with additional reasons. Acceptable reasons (examples) include: (i) electing/changing/discharging an agent within one month of expiry; (ii) changing applicants within one month when adding new applicants; (iii) receiving foreign office examination outcomes within two months and submitting those with the request; (iv) delayed delivery of written ground for rejection by more than one month; (v) pending trial or litigation on related applications; (vi) necessary testing/evaluation related to the ground for rejection; (vii) other unavoidable cases. If a third party files the extension request, reasons (i)-(v) are not admitted. Fees for extension must be paid within a time limit set by the examiner; if unpaid the request is invalidated. If an extension request is filed after the designated period, the applicant is given opportunity to petition and fees are refunded if the request is returned or rejected.

rubrics_metrics.name: Extension and approval of period designated for formality examination
rubrics_metrics.description: Rules for extension of periods designated for formality (e.g., amendments under Article 46).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Extensions can be made several times for a minimum of one month; requests under one month are treated as one month. Total extension available shall not exceed four months, except where further extension is necessary due to reasons not imputable to applicant or international transition. Where extension does not exceed four months and fee is paid, the request is deemed approved on filing; for a four-month extension, a written forewarning 'no further extension will be approved afterward' must be provided. Further extension requests are rejected. Overdue extension requests are returned and fees refunded. Fees refunded where extension request rejected.

rubrics_metrics.name: Shortening designated periods and appeal-related extensions
rubrics_metrics.description: Rules for shortening a designated period and for limited extension of appeal-request periods.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: A request to shorten a designated period or a written amendment indicating desire to shorten leads to the designated period being deemed expired as of the submission date. Any person can request to extend the period for requesting an appeal trial against a decision to reject an application once for up to 30 days; further extension may be allowed for persons in hard-to-access areas upon PTAB review. Written amendments submitted after a designated period are returned as overdue; however, amendments regarding formalities are admitted any time before invalidation.

rubrics_metrics.name: Instructions for written argument — admissibility and examiner duties
rubrics_metrics.description: How examiners should treat written arguments and accompanying amendments submitted in response to grounds for rejection.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Where a written argument is submitted with an amendment, the examiner shall review both in depth and determine whether the notified grounds for rejection can be overcome. Where only a written argument is submitted without amendment, the examiner shall still sufficiently consider the argument. Written arguments and other documents (including experimental results) submitted in response to a notice of grounds for rejection are not part of the specification but may be referred to decide patentability. Amendments submitted after the designated period are returned, but written arguments may be admitted as reference. If an applicant claims amendments in a written argument but fails to submit them, examiner examines based on the existing description and claims; if there is discrepancy between insisted amendments and actual amendment, examiner bases examination on the actual amendment. If matters are disclosed only in the written argument and not in the amendment (indicating requirements are met), examiner may re-notify the same ground for rejection at his/her discretion (see re-notice procedures).

rubrics_metrics.name: Confirmation method for amended specification — multiple amendments handling
rubrics_metrics.description: How the final specification to be examined is determined when multiple amendments are submitted, and differences in treatment depending on filing date and statutory revision.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If multiple voluntary amendments are submitted before any notice of ground for rejection, each amendment is accumulatively reflected and the final specification determined automatically through internal tools. For applications filed before June 30, 2013 (pre-revision), multiple amendments submitted within designated periods are cumulatively reflected; for amendments submitted to final rejection necessitated by amendment, amendments approved by the examiner among all amendments are cumulatively reflected. For applications filed after July 1, 2013 (post-revision Act no. 11654), where multiple amendments are submitted to a ground for rejection within the designated period, all amendments submitted before the final amendment are deemed withdrawn (Article 47(4)); the final specification to be examined is reflected only with the lastly-submitted amendment. A full-text specification amendment replaces the specification to be examined.

rubrics_metrics.name: Treatment when amendment entry is refused
rubrics_metrics.description: If an amendment in response to a final rejection necessitated by amendment or made upon reexamination request is refused entry under Article 52(1), the examiner considers the amendment to have never been submitted.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Refusal to enter amendment will be referred to the section on 'Response to Final Rejection Necessitated by Amendment' and handled as if the refused amendment never existed in the record (i.e., it does not alter the specification to be examined).

rubrics_metrics.name: Additional amendment timing rules and special cases
rubrics_metrics.description: Additional considerations about voluntary amendments, amendments submitted before applicant receives grounds for rejection, and multiple amendments within the designated period.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Voluntary amendments submitted before examination starts and amendments in response to non-final rejection within the designated period are recognized as submitted. For applications filed after July 1, 2013, if more than two amendments to the ground for rejection are submitted within the designated period, all amendments submitted before the final amendment are deemed withdrawn. An applicant may voluntarily amend during the period between an examiner's sending of the grounds for rejection and the applicant's receipt; if parcel registered receipt confirms applicant's receipt date is same as amendment submission date, amendment is regarded as submitted earlier than receipt unless evidence shows delivery preceded amendment. If a written amendment identifies the delivery number of the notice of grounds for rejection, delivery is regarded earlier than amendment submission.

rubrics_metrics.name: Examination outcomes after amendments — decision criteria
rubrics_metrics.description: How an examiner decides to grant, reject, re-notify, or issue final rejection after reviewing amended specifications (single or multiple amendments).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If only Amendment A is submitted: (a) if amended spec discloses no ground for rejection -> decide to grant patent; (b) if amended spec still discloses a previously notified ground -> decide to reject because amendment fails to overcome ground; (c) if previously notified grounds are overcome but a new ground arises due to Amendment A, or a ground existed in the original spec but was not previously notified -> notify the non-final ground again. If Amendments A and B are submitted, same decision logic applies; additionally, if no ground exists but a ground arises from Amendment B, the examiner shall notify the final rejection necessitated by amendment.

rubrics_metrics.name: Requesting reference documents for examination — types and procedure
rubrics_metrics.description: An examiner may ask an applicant to submit documents and other references required for examination to expedite proceedings; the request must state general information and which documents are required.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Examples of requested documents: (i) related documents and translations for international applications and examination outcomes from other offices; (ii) a written statement mapping each claim's technical subject matter to corresponding description paragraphs and explaining relations among claims for applications with voluminous description/claims; (iii) a written statement summarizing the gist of a claimed invention if too complex to comprehend within designated period; (iv) samples or experimental results where effects cannot be verified without them (submission should enable confirmation that the description was definite and sufficient upon filing); (v) written statement explaining process of inducing a formula and definitions/meanings of technical terminology or signs that are unclear; (vi) a written statement clarifying an applicant's claim in written arguments when hard to understand; (vii) documents relevant to examination results of the priority application and their Korean translations. Requests shall be made in the name of the examiner in charge, specifically clarify which document to submit, and designate the submission period within the period for written-argument submission. To expedite examination, examiner may include document requests in the notice of grounds for rejection. For international applications, IPSR/ISR copies may be requested in the Commissioner's name. If an applicant fails to respond, the application shall not be invalidated, but the examiner may instruct re-filing if documents are deficient.

rubrics_metrics.name: Use and limits of submitted documents — reference only
rubrics_metrics.description: Documents submitted by examiner's request are used only as reference material and cannot substitute or supplement the description in the application.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Even if an applicant fails to respond, examiner shall not invalidate the application procedure. The examiner may instruct the applicant to file documents again if required documents are not submitted or are deficient. Documents submitted are for reference in examination but do not become part of the specification.

rubrics_metrics.name: Handling, storage, return, and disposal of submitted documents and samples
rubrics_metrics.description: Procedures for storing, returning, and disposing of documents or samples received from applicants for examination.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: When receiving documents or samples, the examiner shall keep a document list and store them in the file wrapper if possible or separately until examination closes. Examiner must (i) pay special attention to storing return-requested documents/samples undamaged; (ii) also take care for samples/documents with no return request in case they are requested in trial; (iii) commence return procedure right after examination closes. If the submitter intends to get them back, they must state this on the return request form; examiner designates return period and notifies submitter. If no return request is made or the submitter fails to complete return within the designated period, documents or samples may be disposed of as decided by the Commissioner of KIPO.

rubrics_metrics.name: Use of evidential documents as prior art — conditions and cautions
rubrics_metrics.description: When and how evidential documents submitted may be used as prior art during examination.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If evidential documents are periodicals or their copies, or copies of description/drawings published before the application date, an examiner may use them as prior art without additional examination of evidence. For evidential documents other than such periodicals or published copies, an examiner may use them as prior art only if confident of the factual matters without further examination. However, if an applicant argues the existence of an evidential fact in written argument, the examiner shall not admit the fact unless it is justifiable. The Patent Act has no provisions regarding examination of evidence during examination; therefore, where evidential documents are not clearly confirmable, examiner should not decide to reject the application based solely on that evidence.

rubrics_metrics.name: Third-party provision of evidence permitted
rubrics_metrics.description: Anyone (except an incompetent minor without legal representative) may provide relevant evidence to an examiner to argue that a claimed invention should not be patented.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Information provision can be made by any person or corporation; examiner may refer to documents or information provided by a group or association instead of invalidating or returning them. Submitted evidential documents may be used under the conditions stated for evidential documents as prior art.

rubrics_metrics.name: Triggers for additional search
rubrics_metrics.description: Situations in which an examiner shall conduct additional prior-art searches during examination.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Additional searches are required when: (i) the examiner finds via written argument, personal interview, or provided information that incomplete understanding of the claimed invention resulted in an incomplete search; (ii) amended claims include subject matter not covered by the original search; (iii) the examiner intends to examine claimed invention previously excluded from the original search due to lack of unity of invention; (iv) an international patent application that is another application under Article 29(3) enters domestic stage and translation is expected; (v) other cases considered necessary for additional research.

rubrics_metrics.name: Examination deferral or extension of processing period — grounds and procedures
rubrics_metrics.description: When an examiner may defer examination or extend the processing period (within two months) and procedural requirements for such deferral/extension.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: An examiner may defer/extend (within two months) when: (i) a prior-filed application or conflicting applications are not laid open or an examination request for conflicting applications is not made; (ii) the period during which a prior-filed application serving as a basis for domestic priority claim is deemed withdrawn has not elapsed; (iii) a patent trial or proceeding related to the application is pending (includes administrative trial/litigation); (iv) extension required because prior-art search is outsourced, expert opinions are inquired, or consultation examination is needed; (v) the period designated for submission of evidential documents for priority in treaty-claimed applications has not elapsed; (vi) other necessary occasions. Note: deferral/extension not allowed when the Commissioner or examiner designates the processing period. Deferrals/extensions must be reported to the head of the Examination Unit and notified to the applicant. Examiner shall review reasons more than once a month and conduct examination by the termination date if reasons are cleared. If further deferral/extension is needed, report to higher management and limit to two months; additional extension allowed in certain cases not imputable to examiner (e.g., prior-art search report not delivered). When deciding to defer/extend again, the examiner must notify the applicant of specific reasons.

rubrics_metrics.name: Deferral rules for later-filed applications when identical inventions exist
rubrics_metrics.description: How to handle examination start/deferral where multiple applications are filed on the identical invention (prior-filed vs later-filed).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If multiple applications on identical invention exist, the examiner shall defer examination for later-filed applications until the prior-filed application has been processed, laid-open, or registered. However, if the later-filed application can be rejected based on the same ground as the prior-filed application, the examiner can start examination on the later-filed application. Detailed handling depends on whether applicants are identical and whether the prior-filed application is laid-open, with different notification and determination procedures (including applying Article 36(1) or Article 29(3)(iv) where appropriate). If the prior-filed application is later examined/laidover/registered after deferral, the examiner may conduct examination on later-filed application but shall make final decision applying Article 36(1) once the scope of claim of the prior-filed application is determined.
